claim: The whole Trotter step compiles to exactly 54 MS gates at infidelity <= 1e-4 by resynthesizing each block to its known per-block MS minimum: fit ONE canonical 3-qubit hopping block (HOP_UNITARY) to a 4-MS native ansatz, replicate it to all 12 identical hopping blocks by qubit relabelling, and realize each of the 6 on-site blocks (INT_UNITARY) as a single MS gate. Plain version: Dhruv's ideal step is built from 12 copies of the same little 3-qubit operation plus 6 tiny 2-qubit ones; if we hand-optimize the 3-qubit one down to 4 entangling gates ONCE and stamp it everywhere, plus 1 gate each for the small ones, we get 12x4 + 6x1 = 54 entangling gates -- exactly matching his hand-designed 9N=54, and far below our 102 baseline.
prediction: build_circuit() returns a native-only circuit with ms_count == 54 and estimate_infidelity <= 1e-4 (expected ~1e-8 or better, since the exact per-block minimum is 4 MS so fit_block should reach ~1e-12 on the single hopping block and the 12 near-machine-precision blocks compose additively to well under 1e-4). Blinded score = 54, promoting over the 102-MS incumbent and tying Dhruv's hand-optimized 9N.
falsifier: Any of: (a) fit_block cannot drive the single 3-qubit HOP_UNITARY below ~1e-6 infidelity at n_ms=4 across many restarts (would contradict the stated exact 4-MS-per-block minimum); (b) the composed 54-MS circuit's self-checked estimate_infidelity exceeds 1e-4 despite each block fitting well below it (would mean per-block errors do NOT compose additively / there is a qubit-order or remap bug); (c) is_native fails or ms_count != 54.
kill_threshold: Abandon this exact-resynthesis route if, after restarts>=60 and a seed sweep, the canonical HOP block 4-MS fit stalls above 1e-6, OR the assembled circuit's estimate_infidelity stays above 1e-4. In that case the '4 MS exact per hopping block' premise is wrong for this ruler and the next hypothesis must either raise the hopping-block MS budget (n_ms=5) or attack the composition/order rather than re-run per-block fitting.
brief:
Edit ONLY workspace/candidate.py. Goal: a self-contained build_circuit() -> list of native-gate tuples with exactly 54 MS gates matching U_ideal (ideal_step) to estimate_infidelity <= 1e-4. candidate.py is scored as a COPY in experiments/ where target/baseline are NOT importable, so you MUST freeze all numeric angles into candidate.py; numpy is allowed, importing target is not.

STEP 1 (generate, in the workspace where target IS importable -- a throwaway scratch script, delete after): import target as T. Fit the canonical hopping block once:
  hop_circ, hop_inf = T.fit_block(T.HOP_UNITARY, [0,1,2], n_ms=4, restarts=60, seed=0, tol=1e-12)
HOP_UNITARY is 8x8 on local order [tau, a, b]. If hop_inf > 1e-8, re-run sweeping seed in {0,1,2,3,7} and take the best; you need hop_inf comfortably below 1e-8 (ideally ~1e-12). hop_circ is a native gate list on qubits {0,1,2} (GPi/GPi2/RZ singles + 4 MS).

STEP 2: verify the on-site block is a single MS analytically: MS(0,0,theta) = expm(-i*theta/2 * X kron X) and INT_UNITARY = expm(-i*DT*(U/2)*X kron X), so INT_UNITARY == ms(0.0,0.0,DT*U) with DT*U = 0.6. Assert np.allclose(T.ms(0.0,0.0,0.6), T.INT_UNITARY, atol=1e-12) in scratch. The on-site gate on global qubits [q0,q1] is ('MS', q0, q1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.6).

STEP 3 (freeze into candidate.py): paste hop_circ as a module-level constant HOP_GATES = [ ...exact tuples on local qubits 0,1,2... ] (round-trip the actual float values; do not re-import target). Reproduce the FROZEN layout arithmetic locally (no import): N=6; m_up=lambda i:3*(i%N); m_dn=lambda i:3*(i%N)+1; tau=lambda b:3*(b%N)+2; hop_qubits(b) returns ([tau(b), m_up(b), m_up((b+1)%N)], [tau(b), m_dn(b), m_dn((b+1)%N)]); int_qubits(i) returns [tau((i-1)%N), tau(i)]. Add a remap helper: remap(gates, gmap) rewrites each gate's qubit slot(s) via gmap (single-qubit gates ('GPi'/'GPi2'/'RZ', q, ang) -> q=gmap[q]; ('MS', q0, q1, p0, p1, th) -> gmap[q0], gmap[q1]).

STEP 4: build_circuit() MUST emit blocks in the SAME order as ideal_step (blocks share qubits, so order is load-bearing): for b in range(6): emit remap(HOP_GATES, {0:qa[0],1:qa[1],2:qa[2]}) then remap(HOP_GATES, {0:qb[0],1:qb[1],2:qb[2]}) where qa,qb = hop_qubits(b). THEN for i in range(6): emit ('MS', int_qubits(i)[0], int_qubits(i)[1], 0.0, 0.0, 0.6). Return the concatenated list.

STEP 5 (self-check, scratch): assert T.is_native(cand)[0]; assert T.ms_count(cand)==54; assert T.estimate_infidelity(cand) <= 1e-4 (print it). Then delete the scratch script (throwaway means throwaway). Do not touch any file other than candidate.py.
done_definition: workspace/candidate.py defines a self-contained build_circuit() (no import of target/baseline/incumbent) that returns a native-only gate list with ms_count exactly 54, is_native True, and estimate_infidelity(build_circuit()) <= 1e-4 verified locally; all hopping-block angles and the on-site MS angle are hardcoded numeric literals; no file other than candidate.py is modified.
reopen_condition: If this dies because the 4-MS canonical hopping-block fit stalls above 1e-6 (premise b/c false for this ruler), reopen ONLY when a new fact lowers the per-block floor: a specific working (pairs, n_ms) structure for the 3-qubit hopping block certified below 1e-6 at 4 MS, OR a Director revision of the '4 MS exact per hopping block' claim. Do not re-run identical fit_block calls hoping for a better local minimum without changed structure.
